chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
A man must not harm his wife when he divorces her by straitening her (financially) until she moves out before the expiration of her waiting period.
For indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has forbidden that.
And do not injure them in order to straiten them.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on financially straitening a divorced wife before her waiting period ends?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the practical application of Quranic injunctions by prohibiting husbands from using financial pressure to force their wives to relinquish their right to remain in the marital home during the 'iddah' period. It underscores the Shia legal principle that 'not injuring' (la yudarru) extends beyond mere physical harm to include economic coercion, ensuring the wife's dignity and stability until the waiting period concludes. This ruling reinforces the Quranic command in Surah At-Talaq to treat divorced women with kindness and fairness, preventing the husband from exploiting his financial control to expedite the divorce process.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The man must not harm his wife when he divorces her, so he (financially) straitens upon her until she moves before the fulfillment of her waiting period,
for Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic has Forbidden from that,
so Heazwj Said [65:6] and do not injure them in order that you may straiten them’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabiy who has said the following: “Abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
A man must not harm his wife when he divorces her to make it difficult for her so she is forced to move away before the end of her waiting period.
Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, has prohibited it, saying, . .

you must not harm them (women) to make it difficult for them.’” [65:6] Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn abu Hamzah from abu Basir from abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, a similar Hadith.
